survivingNetNew.title: Pausing the dispatcher does not freeze custody: release()/rescueERC20() are not whenNotPaused, so held USDC can still leave during a pause
survivingNetNew.summary: dispatch() is whenNotPaused but the custody-moving release() (onlyReleaser) and rescueERC20() (onlyOwner) are not pause-gated. Pausing halts the inbound mint/debt-accrual side only; a whitelisted releaser can keep moving held USDC to batchMinter mid-pause. No theft and no unbacked phUSD (release only relocates already-held backing to its intended sink; releasers are owner-curated). Surfaced as a Law-3 non-obvious operational footgun with safe-config guidance (revoke releasers to actually freeze custody). rescueERC20 being un-gated during pause is explicitly intended (escape hatch) and is correct.
survivingNetNew.lawNote: Law 3 footgun (non-obvious pause semantics). Owner/releasers trusted; report as operational hazard, do not escalate.
survivingNetNew.ledgerCollision: NONE — distinct contract+function+root-cause. Conceptually ADJACENT to open L-04 (49fb985f… 'mintFor()/burn() ignore global paused + per-index disabled flags', NFTMinterV2) which is the same 'privileged path ignores pause flag' family, but L-04 is a value-MINTING bypass on a different live contract, while this is a custody-freeze-expectation gap on the new story-043 dispatcher. Distinct fingerprint; cross-reference only, DO NOT merge.
survivingNetNew.dispositionNote: Borderline reportable Low; include with safe-config guidance, qa-bundle. Surface for owner triage; do not auto-suppress.

survivingNetNew.title: Delay-release variant drops the sibling NudgeRatchet's in-contract require(bal >= amount) backing tripwire from _dispatch, relocating the 'no unbacked phUSD' invariant off-contract into NFTMinterV2's measured actualReceived
survivingNetNew.summary: The sibling NudgeRatchet._dispatch re-asserts require(bal >= amount) ('the one direction that mints unbacked phUSD'); this variant's _dispatch is a view no-op that holds rather than sweeps and performs no balance read / no assertion. SAFE in the shipped wiring: NFTMinterV2._executeMint transfers USDC directly to the dispatcher and dispatches exactly the measured balance-delta (actualReceived), and dispatch is onlyMinter — so accrued mint-debt always equals on-contract USDC by construction. The dropped check is therefore redundant today and there is NO live exploit. Latent only under a non-default setMinter repoint to a minter that does not replicate the measured-delta discipline. QA, not Medium.
survivingNetNew.lawNote: Law-3 borderline footgun surfaced honestly at QA: a competent owner could assume this dispatcher self-defends the backing invariant the way its near-identical sibling does and reuse it in a new wiring. Not a malicious-owner vector, not a live bug.
survivingNetNew.recommendation: Cheaply restore parity: read IERC20(_token).balanceOf(address(this)) in _dispatch and require(bal >= amount) (stays view; trivially satisfied in the honest held-balance path).
survivingNetNew.ledgerCollision: DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from DEDUP-001 (070fdf42…, suppressed). Per econ-scanner's explicit instruction, ECON-001 is NARROWER than DEDUP-001: it concerns an in-contract on-chain assertion that the sibling enforces and this variant drops, NOT the external phUSD backing model. DO NOT collapse ECON-001 into DEDUP-001's suppression. No collision with L-08 (0b97f155…, fixed) — that variant lacked rescue; this one adds it.
survivingNetNew.dispositionNote: Surface for owner triage at QA; flag for human review on the collapse boundary vs DEDUP-001 (econ-scanner says keep separate).
